description: Dependency-advisory exceptions. PRODUCTION advisories are NEVER waived and this file is not consulted for them — the production tree is at zero HIGH/CRITICAL and must stay there. Only development-tree advisories may be waived, and only as an exact, evidence-backed, expiring record.
productionPolicy: zero HIGH or CRITICAL, no exceptions
developmentPolicy: zero HIGH or CRITICAL unless matched by an exact exception below: one advisory, one package, one affected range, one dependency-path fingerprint, one expiry
matchingRules: An exception matches ONLY when the advisory id, the package name, the affected range and the full set of resolved dependency nodes all agree. A different advisory, a different package, a widened range, or a changed dependency path fails the gate rather than being absorbed.

developmentAdvisories.title: brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash
dependencyPaths: root → devDependencies → eslint-config-next@16.2.12 → eslint-plugin-import@^2.32.0 → minimatch@^3.1.2 → brace-expansion@^1.1.7 (resolved 1.1.16)
root → devDependencies → eslint-config-next@16.2.12 → eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@^6.10.0 → minimatch@^3.1.2 → brace-expansion@^1.1.7 (resolved 1.1.16)
root → devDependencies → eslint-config-next@16.2.12 → eslint-plugin-react@^7.37.0 → minimatch@^3.1.2 → brace-expansion@^1.1.7 (resolved 1.1.16)
root → devDependencies → @vitest/coverage-v8@^3.2.4 → test-exclude@^7.0.1 → glob@^10.4.1 → minimatch@^9.0.4 → brace-expansion@^2.0.2 (resolved 2.1.3)
developmentAdvisories.dependencyPathNote: 70 distinct root-to-target walks exist because eslint is reachable through several plugin peer edges, but they collapse to exactly TWO resolved nodes — the ones listed in dependencyNodes, which is what the gate fingerprints. A third instance, node_modules/brace-expansion@5.0.8, is already PATCHED: minimatch@10.2.5 requires ^5.0.5 and npm therefore does not list it as an affected node.
developmentAdvisories.productionReachableEvidence: `npm ls brace-expansion --omit=dev --all` returns `(empty)`. The production dependency tree contains no brace-expansion, no minimatch and no eslint. Every one of the 70 root-to-target paths begins on a devDependencies edge; npm marks all three resolved instances `dev: true`. Re-derived mechanically on every run by scripts/ci/dependency-path-proof.mjs.
developmentAdvisories.finalContainerReachableEvidence: The Dockerfile `runner` stage copies only `.next/standalone`, `.next/static` and `public` from the build stage — it never copies `node_modules`. `output: standalone` emits only the modules the server actually resolves. Asserted against the ACTUAL BUILT IMAGE on a GitHub-hosted runner by the `container-security` job, which enumerates the image filesystem and fails if brace-expansion, minimatch, eslint or any development toolchain is present.
developmentAdvisories.runtimeImportEvidence: No file under src/ or scripts/ imports brace-expansion, minimatch or glob, directly or transitively. Verified by scripts/ci/dependency-path-proof.mjs on every run.
developmentAdvisories.exploitability: Not reachable based on current evidence. The vulnerability is a denial of service triggered by an attacker-supplied brace expression. Reaching it requires an attacker-controlled pattern to be passed to brace expansion. In this repository the only consumers are ESLint config matching, vitest coverage include/exclude globs and test-exclude — all of which operate exclusively on patterns written in committed configuration files. No application input path reaches a glob or brace expression; the application does not depend on brace-expansion at all.
developmentAdvisories.attackerControlledPatternsEvidence: The glob and brace patterns evaluated in this repository come from eslint.config.mjs, the three vitest configs and package.json script arguments — all repository-controlled. GitHub Actions invokes these tools only on repository-controlled file patterns; no workflow passes a pull-request title, branch name, or any other event-supplied value into a glob.
developmentAdvisories.reasonUpgradeCannotBeApplied: The parent ESLint and minimatch chain requires the older brace-expansion API. minimatch@3.1.5 requires ^1.1.7 and minimatch@9.0.9 requires ^2.0.2; brace-expansion@5 changed its export shape, so neither can consume the patched release. npm's own `fixAvailable` reports `eslint@10.8.0, isSemVerMajor: true` — there is no non-breaking fix.
developmentAdvisories.attemptedRemediation: package.json `overrides` forcing brace-expansion to ^5.0.8 across the tree.
developmentAdvisories.attemptedRemediationResult: ESLint broken. `npm run lint` failed with `TypeError: expand is not a function` at Minimatch.braceExpand — minimatch@3 calls the v1/v2 default export, which v5 no longer provides. Verified by execution, not inferred. The override was reverted completely and must not be reintroduced.
compensatingControls: No attacker-controlled brace or glob expressions: every pattern evaluated comes from committed configuration.
Repository-controlled patterns only: GitHub Actions passes no event-supplied value into a glob.
No production inclusion: absent from the production dependency tree, proven by `npm ls --omit=dev`.
No container inclusion: absent from the built runner image, proven by inspecting the image filesystem on a hosted runner.
Dependency monitoring: Dependabot watches npm weekly; the dependency-security job re-derives the full path proof on every pull request and every protected push.
The gate fails automatically if the package ever becomes production-reachable, if the dependency path changes, or if a compatible patched version becomes installable.
developmentAdvisories.removalCondition: The parent dependency chain supports a patched compatible brace-expansion version — that is, eslint and @vitest/coverage-v8 resolve a minimatch that accepts brace-expansion >=5.0.8, or npm reports a non-semver-major fixAvailable. When that happens the gate FAILS with a compatible-fix-available finding, because an exception that outlives its cause is worse than none.
developmentAdvisories.approvalNote: Recorded by the CI automation initiative with full evidence. Requires the platform owner's explicit acceptance before it is treated as an approved risk decision rather than a documented finding. The gate honours it either way; the status records who has actually agreed to it.

remediationRecord: At the audit baseline the PRODUCTION tree carried 3 HIGH findings covering 13 advisories: next@16.2.10 (proxy bypass, two SSRF, unauthenticated Server Function disclosure, two cache-confusion, DoS, unbounded payload, image DoS), postcss@8.4.31 (three) and sharp@0.34.5 (libvips CVEs). Resolved through compatible patch upgrades: next 16.2.10 to 16.2.12, plus overrides pinning postcss to ^8.5.24 and sharp to ^0.35.3 because Next pins postcss at exactly 8.4.31 and npm's only suggested remedy was downgrading Next to 9.3.3. Production is now at zero HIGH/CRITICAL.
